narrative:
On August 12, 2026, the Karnataka High Court recorded an overall hearing rate of 40.2%, successfully hearing 1,073 out of 2,670 scheduled matters across 51 judges. This reflects a slight dip in percentage efficiency compared to the prior day, August 11, which saw a 41.2% hearing rate (1,066 heard out of 2,589 scheduled), though the total volume of heard cases increased. Today's performance remains higher than the 39.6% rate recorded on August 7, but trails the 45.6% conversion achieved on August 6.

Judicial throughput varied based on docket load across court halls. Justice S. Vishwajith Shetty in Hall 19 managed the heaviest individual list of 326 cases, hearing 109 (33.4%). Justice V. Srishananda in Hall 21 demonstrated strong conversion by taking up 63 of 97 scheduled cases (64.9%). Justice Shivashankar Amarannavar in Hall 20 achieved consistently high hearing rates across multiple lists, including 86.4% (19 of 22) and 80.0% (20 of 25). In Hall 14, Justice M. Nagaprasanna converted 51 of 154 matters (33.1%) on a major list alongside 32 of 50 matters (64.0%) on a secondary list.

By procedural stage, Orders comprised the largest scheduled volume, with 341 of 814 cases heard (41.9%), followed by Preliminary Hearings at 41.4% (196 of 474) and Admissions at 39.6% (218 of 551). Final Hearings logged a lower conversion rate of 23.3% (119 of 510). Workload distribution was heavily concentrated in Writ Petitions (WP), which accounted for 1,193 scheduled cases with 459 heard (38.5%). Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) recorded a 43.3% clearance rate (151 of 349), while Regular Second Appeals (RSA) achieved a high conversion rate of 65.2% (75 of 115).
